title: Aliens-Trick Job Split
insight: You must pick **exactly k** disjoint intervals maximizing value; the per-k DP is O(nk). **Lagrangian/"Aliens" trick**: the answer-as-function-of-k is convex, so binary-search a penalty λ added per interval, drop the k-dimension to O(n), then recover k.
io: `n k` then `n` ints (interval value array) → max value with exactly k picks
oracle: brute O(nk) DP on n≤200, cross-check

title: Divide-and-Conquer-Optimization Mailboxes
insight: Place p mailboxes on a line to minimize sum of distances; the cost matrix satisfies the **Monge/quadrangle inequality**, so the optimal split point is monotonic → divide-and-conquer optimization turns O(pn²) into O(pn log n).
io: `n p` then n sorted positions → min total distance

title: Knuth-Opt Optimal BST-ish Merge
insight: Interval DP for optimal merge cost is O(n³); the cost is Monge, so **Knuth's optimal-split monotonicity** `opt[i][j-1] ≤ opt[i][j] ≤ opt[i+1][j]` collapses it to O(n²).
io: `n` then n weights → min merge cost

title: Bitmask-over-Profile Broken Grid
insight: Tile/count over an h×w grid with h≤14: naive 2^(hw) is hopeless. **Broken-profile DP** carries the contour as one (h+1)-bit mask processed cell-by-cell, O(w·h·2^h).

title: Connected-Component DP on Trees ("rerooting count")
insight: Count labeled ways under a subtree constraint; the naive is per-root O(n²). **Rerooting**: compute the answer for one root, then push parent-contributions in a second pass for O(n).
io: `n` then n−1 edges → vector of n answers

title: SOS (Subset-Sum-over-Subsets) Pairing
insight: Count pairs (i,j) with `a[i] AND a[j] == 0` (disjoint bitmasks). Brute is O(n²). **Sum-over-subsets DP** over the 2^B mask lattice computes, for each mask, the count of array values that are submasks, in O(B·2^B).
io: `n` then n ints <2^20 → count of disjoint pairs

title: Digit DP with Carry State
insight: Count integers in [L,R] whose decimal digits sum to a multiple of their length-dependent modulus — a *non-local* digit property. **Digit DP** carrying (position, running mod, tight-flag) makes it O(digits·mod·2).

title: Project Selection (Max-Weight Closure)
insight: "Pick projects to maximize profit, but each project requires prerequisite machines that cost money" reads like a knapsack; it is exactly **max-weight closure → min-cut**: source→profit nodes, cost nodes→sink, prerequisite edges ∞; answer = Σpositive − mincut.
io: `n m` profits, then prerequisite edges → max profit

title: Tournament Scheduling as 2-SAT
insight: Each constraint "team i plays home XOR team j plays home in round r" plus implications is a tangle of boolean constraints. **Model as 2-SAT**, build implication graph, SCC; satisfiable iff no var and its negation share an SCC.

title: Min-Cost Flow Disguised as Assignment-with-Quotas
insight: Workers→tasks with per-worker quotas and convex overtime cost looks like Hungarian; the convex cost breaks Hungarian. **Successive-shortest-path MCMF** with per-unit edges encodes the convex cost as parallel increasing-cost unit edges.
io: bipartite costs + quotas → min total cost

title: Eulerian-Circuit Reconstruction (de Bruijn)
insight: "Reassemble a string from all its overlapping k-mers" is not DP — it is finding an **Eulerian path in the de Bruijn graph** of (k−1)-mers; Hierholzer in O(E).
io: `k` then list of k-mers → one valid superstring or `IMPOSSIBLE`
oracle: verify output contains all k-mers; brute on tiny

title: Bridges → Biconnected 2-Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
insight: "Add fewest edges so the network has no single point of failure" — find bridges (Tarjan low-link), contract 2-edge-connected components into a tree, answer = ⌈leaves/2⌉. The ⌈leaves/2⌉ formula is the non-obvious step.

title: Shortest Path on a State-Product Graph (0-1 BFS)
insight: Grid with "you may flip ≤1 wall" — don't run Dijkstra ad hoc; build the **layered graph** (cell × flips-used) and run **0-1 BFS** (deque) since edge weights ∈{0,1}, giving O(VE)→O(V).
oracle: Dijkstra on same state graph as cross-check

title: Functional-Graph Cycle Arithmetic
insight: Each node has exactly one out-edge `f(i)`; answer queries "where after t steps" with t up to 1e18. **Decompose into ρ-shape (tail + cycle)**, jump the tail, then mod into the cycle — *not* binary lifting (too much memory at this scale).

title: Auxiliary (Virtual) Tree Queries
insight: Many queries each give a subset S of ≤... nodes and ask a tree-DP over them; redoing DP on the full tree per query is O(qn). **Build the virtual tree** of S (sorted by Euler-in time + LCAs) so each query costs O(
oracle: `n` edges, q queries each a node-set → per-query answer

title: Centroid Decomposition Path Counting
insight: Count paths with length exactly L; per-pair is O(n²). **Centroid decomposition**: every path passes through some centroid; count cross-centroid pairs with a frequency array, recurse → O(n log n).

title: Small-to-Large (DSU on tree) Color Queries
insight: For each subtree report #distinct colors; naive per-subtree is O(n²). **Small-to-large / DSU-on-tree**: keep heavy child's structure, re-add only light children → O(n log n).

title: Re-rooting Sum-of-Distances
insight: Sum of distances from *every* node; the O(n²) BFS-from-each is too slow. **Two-pass rerooting**: subtree sizes give the root's answer, then `ans[child]=ans[par]+(n−2·size[child])` propagates in O(n). The transfer formula is the insight.

title: Heavy-Light + Segment Tree on Path XOR
insight: Path-update / path-query with XOR-assignment can't be plain LCA prefix because of updates. **HLD** decomposes each path into O(log n) chains, each a segment-tree range; combine. The "XOR-assign is range-affine" observation enables lazy.
io: `n` edges, q mixed ops → query answers

title: Tree Isomorphism by Canonical Hashing
insight: "Are two rooted forests structurally equal?" — string-equality on serialization is wrong (sibling order). **Canonical AHU hashing**: hash each node from the *sorted multiset* of children hashes; equal canonical roots ⇔ isomorphic.

title: Distinct Substrings via Suffix Automaton
insight: Count distinct substrings; the O(n²) enumerate-and-hash dies at 1e6. **Suffix automaton**: #distinct substrings = Σ over states `(len[s]−len[link[s]])`, built online in O(n).

title: Z-Function "Border-Forced" Compression
insight: "Shortest string whose self-overlap matches a given overlap profile" — reverse-engineer from the **Z/prefix-function**; the constraint that borders compose transitively is the non-obvious feasibility test.

title: Aho-Corasick Multi-Pattern Weighting
insight: Score a text by total weight of all dictionary-pattern occurrences; running each pattern's KMP is O(text·patterns). **Aho-Corasick** automaton + fail-tree subtree-sum makes it O(text + Σpattern).

title: Palindromic Factorization (eertree)
insight: Min #palindromes to partition s; per-position O(n) palindrome check is O(n²). **Palindromic tree (eertree)** gives all distinct palindromic suffixes incrementally → O(n log n) DP via series-links.

title: Lyndon / Booth Minimal Rotation
insight: Find the lexicographically least rotation; the O(n²) compare-all-rotations is too slow. **Booth's algorithm** (or Duval/Lyndon factorization) finds it in O(n) by a clever failure-function-like scan — the "skip a whole block on mismatch" step is the insight.

title: CRT Reconstruction with Inconsistency
insight: "Find x ≡ rᵢ (mod mᵢ)" with **non-coprime** moduli; textbook CRT assumes coprime. The insight is the **merge rule that checks `(r₁−r₂) divisible by gcd(m₁,m₂)`** and combines via lcm, returning −1 on contradiction.

title: Mod-Inverse-Free Combinatorics (Lucas / prime-power)
insight: nCr mod m where m is **not prime** (or prime power) — Fermat-inverse fails. **Lucas for primes, Andrew Granville / factor-and-Legendre for prime powers**, then CRT. Recognizing inverses don't exist is the trap.

title: Divisor-Sum via Hyperbola Trick
insight: Σ_{i=1..n} (n div i) (or d(i)) for n up to 1e12; the O(n) loop is too slow. **Block decomposition / √n hyperbola method**: floor(n/i) takes only O(√n) distinct values, sum each block in O(1).

title: Pollard-Rho + Miller-Rabin Factor Queries
insight: Factor up to 1e18 fast; trial division to √n=1e9 is too slow. **Miller-Rabin** primality + **Pollard-Rho ρ** with Brent's cycle detection + `__int128` mulmod. The combination + correct deterministic MR witnesses is the insight.

title: Rotating Calipers Max-Width Pair
insight: Farthest pair of points (diameter); all-pairs is O(n²). **Convex hull + rotating calipers**: the diameter is between hull antipodal points, found in one O(n) sweep after the hull.

title: Half-Plane Intersection Feasibility
insight: "Is there a point satisfying all m linear inequalities?" — don't LP-solve generally. **Half-plane intersection** by angular sort + deque; empty intersection ⇔ infeasible. The deque-pop invariant is the insight.

title: Closest Pair by Sweepline + Set
insight: Closest pair; divide-and-conquer is classic but fiddly. **Sweepline with an ordered set window of width = current best d**: only O(1) amortized candidates per point → O(n log n), simpler to get exactly right.

title: Pick's-Theorem Lattice Count
insight: "Count lattice points strictly inside a polygon" — don't scan the bounding box (too big). **Pick's theorem** `A = I + B/2 − 1` with shoelace area A and boundary points B via gcd of edge deltas → I in O(vertices).

title: Offline Range-Distinct (Mo's algorithm)
insight: "#distinct in [l,r]" over many queries; per-query rescan is O(qn). **Mo's algorithm**: sort queries by (block of l, r), move pointers with O(1) add/remove of a count array → O((n+q)√n). The √n block ordering is the insight.

title: Persistent Segment Tree k-th in Range
insight: "k-th smallest in [l,r]" without updates; a merge-sort tree is O(log²). **Persistent segment tree** keyed by value, version per prefix; subtract versions r−(l−1) and descend → O(log n) per query. The prefix-version subtraction is the trick.

title: Li Chao Tree / CHT on a Non-Obvious Cost
insight: A DP `dp[i]=min_j(dp[j]+b[j]·a[i])` looks O(n²); the transition is a set of **lines evaluated at a[i]** → **convex-hull trick / Li Chao tree** gives O(n log n). Recognizing the linear-in-a[i] form is the whole game.

title: Wavelet Tree Range-Rank
insight: "How many elements in [l,r] are ≤ x" for many queries; an offline BIT works but the problem forbids offline (online, forced by XOR-encoded queries). **Wavelet tree** answers rank/quantile online in O(log σ).

title: DSU with Rollback + Offline Dynamic Connectivity
insight: "Are u,v connected at time t?" with edge add/remove — DSU has no delete. **Segment-tree-on-time + DSU with rollback (union by rank only)**: each edge lives on an interval, push to log nodes, DFS with undo. The rollback (no path compression) is the insight.

title: Fenwick of Sorted-Lists "BIT-of-BIT" 2D
insight: 2D dominance counting with updates; a static merge-sort tree fails under updates. **BIT indexed by x, each node a BIT/ordered structure over y** (or offline + BIT-on-compressed-y). The product-structure decomposition is the insight.

title: Scheduling by an Exchange-Argument Comparator
insight: Order jobs (aᵢ,bᵢ) to minimize a coupled cost; the right order is **sort by the pairwise exchange comparator** (e.g. Johnson's rule / `aᵢbⱼ < aⱼbᵢ`), provably optimal by a swap argument — *not* "sort by aᵢ" or "by bᵢ".

title: Lexicographically-Smallest via Monotonic Stack
insight: "Delete k chars to make the smallest string" — greedy "delete largest" is wrong. **Monotonic stack**: pop while top > current and budget remains; the stack invariant *is* the proof.

title: Binary-Search-the-Answer + Greedy Feasibility
insight: "Max-min: place k items so the minimum gap is largest" — direct optimization is hard. **Binary search the answer x**, then a linear greedy checks "can we place k with all gaps ≥ x". Monotonic feasibility is the insight.

title: Median-Minimizes-L1 Meeting Point
insight: "Choose a point minimizing total Manhattan distance to all" — *not* the mean. The **median per axis** minimizes Σ
constraints: ; the separability of L1 across axes is the non-obvious step.

title: Hall's-Theorem Greedy Matching Feasibility
insight: "Can each request be served given interval availabilities?" — a greedy + **Hall's condition** check (sort, assign earliest-deadline) rather than full bipartite matching; the EDF exchange argument proves optimality.

title: Parity-Invariant Reachability
insight: "Can configuration A reach B under these moves?" — simulation is exponential. The moves preserve an **invariant (e.g. parity of inversions / a coloring sum mod k)**; reachable ⇔ invariants match. Finding the invariant is the entire problem (cf. 15-puzzle).
oracle: BFS over states on tiny configs

title: Constructive: Build a Graph with Exact Property
insight: "Output any graph on n nodes with exactly k triangles" — not search. A **constructive recipe** (greedy clique-stacking: each added node into the largest clique adds a known count) hits any feasible k; recognizing the count formula is the insight.
oracle: verify output has exactly k triangles

title: XOR-Basis Linear Algebra over GF(2)
insight: "Max XOR-subset" / "is x representable" — greedy by value is wrong. Build a **linear basis (Gaussian elimination over GF(2))**; max XOR by greedily including basis vectors high-bit-first. The vector-space reformulation is the insight.

title: Game / Sprague-Grundy Nim-Value
insight: "Who wins this take-away game on independent piles?" — direct minimax is exponential. Compute **Grundy numbers per pile (mex of reachable)**, XOR them; nonzero ⇔ first player wins. Decomposing into independent games + Sprague-Grundy is the insight.

title: Guess Permutation by ≤ n log n Comparisons
insight: Recover a hidden permutation using a query oracle (`? i j` returns sign); naive is O(n²) queries. **Divide-and-conquer / merge-sort query schedule** hits O(n log n) — the query-budget reformulation as a sorting lower bound is the insight.
io: interactive: `? i j` ↔ response; final `! perm`
oracle: local judge simulates oracle + counts queries

title: Binary-Search a Hidden Threshold with Lies
insight: Find a hidden value when up to 1 answer may be a lie. **Ternary/redundant binary search** (Rényi–Ulam): each step encodes a parity check so one lie is detectable/correctable; plain binary search fails.
